FROM:  Adrian Fajardo, Management Analyst

SUBJECT: Discussion on Upcoming Coffee with the Captain Events

BACKGROUND
“Coffee with a Cop” was launched in Hawthorne, California in 2011 when Officers from the
Hawthorne Police Department were looking for ways to interact more successfully with the
citizens they served each day. Community policing has long been considered a framework for
establishing trust between the community and the police. However, over time the character
and composition of our nation’s communities have changed due to shifting demographics,
more commuters, and the introduction of different communication methods such as websites
and social media. The Hawthorne Police Department hit upon a simple plan to break through
the barriers that have been built over the years – a cup of coffee.

The City of Artesia held its first Coffee with a Cop event on July 2012. Since then these events
have expanded across the country. The key to Coffee with a Cop’s growing success is that it
opens the door for interactions outside of the crisis situations that typically bring law
enforcement officers and community members together. These events provide opportunities
for law enforcement and community members to come together and discuss local issues and
learn more about each other.

ANALYSIS
The City of Artesia will hold the first Coffee with the Captain event of the year on April 18, 2023
at Solid Coffee Roasters. The restaurant is located at 12147 South St. Artesia, CA. The event
will take place from 8:00 a.m. to 10:00 a.m. Complimentary coffee and pastries will be provided
courtesy of Solid Coffee Roasters. These events are part of the City of Artesia’s ongoing efforts
to improve trust and build relationships with the community.

The City intends to hold three events each calendar year, with the next two occurring in early
summer and the fall. If members of the Commission are interested in assisting with planning
the upcoming events, an ad-hoc committee of two Commissioners may be formed to assist
with program planning. Staff also hope all members of the Commission can attend the event
to assist law enforcement with educating more community members on Neighborhood Watch
Programs and to hear resident concerns regarding safety.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the Public Safety Commission discuss upcoming the Coffee with the
Captain event on April 18th and provide direction for future events.

ATTACHMENTS
Flyer for April 18th Coffee with the Captain Event

SUBJECT: Discussion of Priority Setting for Public Safety Commission Goals and Objectives

BACKGROUND
The Artesia Public Safety Commission is responsible for making recommendations to the City
Council on matters affecting public health and safety in the City. The purpose of this discussion
is to assist City Management and the Commission in carrying out the City Council’s vision and
implementing the City’s Safer Neighborhoods Program.

ANALYSIS
In 2021, the City complied all its public safety related programs under one Safer
Neighborhoods Program (the “Program”). The Program was created as a community
awareness campaign aimed at increasing public participation in public safety and emergency
preparedness. The Program is separated into two components: Public Safety and Emergency
Preparedness.

Some of the initiatives of the Program include:

  Public Safety
  •  Neighborhood Watch Program/Block Captains
  •  Making wellness resources accessible at City parks
  •  Home Security and Alarm Rebate Program

  Emergency Preparedness
  •  Earthquake Preparedness
  •  Fire Prevention Readiness
  •  Community Emergency Response Training (CERT)

In an effort to affirm the City’s mission, vision, and values regarding Public Safety, The
Commission is requested to establish priorities and a work plan to address the Program
objectives. Staff is specifically interested in facilitating a process to improve upon the
community awareness and participation in programs like Neighborhood Watch and CERT.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the Public Safety Commission review the Safer Neighborhoods
Program as outlined in the attached agenda report, and provide feedback to Staff regarding
ways to increase public awareness and engagement in public safety and emergency
preparedness.

ATTACHMENTS
City Council Agenda Report - Safer Neighborhoods Program

   CITY COUNCIL AGENDA REPORT
  MEETING DATE: 8/9/2021  ITEM NO:

 TO:  Mayor and Members of the City Council

 SUBJECT: Receive and File Informational Item on the Safer Neighborhoods Program

 FROM:  Eric Joseph, Management Analyst
  Melissa Burk, Administrative Manager

 REVIEWED AND APPROVED BY:
  William Rawlings, City Manager

RECOMMENDATION:
Staff recommends the City Council receive and file this informational report.

BACKGROUND:
On August 3, 2021, the City hosted its annual National Night Out (NNO) community event.
Traditionally, National Night Out provides residents and public safety officers with an
environment that fosters strong, positive relationships and promotes partnership building
to make neighborhoods safer and more caring places to live. This year’s NNO differed
from past events in one key aspect, the Safer Neighborhoods Program was introduced.
In addition to launching the Program at NNO, concurrently at the August Council Meeting,
the City Council is considering an item to proclaim August 2021 as Safer Neighborhoods
month to further increase community awareness for the Program.

ANALYSIS:
The Safer Neighborhoods Program is a community awareness campaign aimed at getting
more resident participation in public safety and emergency preparedness programs. A
breakdown of the Program areas is found below.

Safer Neighborhoods Program

Public Safety

  1) Neighborhood Watch Program/Block Captains – Encouraging residents to
  become more involved with neighborhood watch is a major goal of the Safer
  Neighborhoods Program. This includes but is not limited to the following activities:
   •  Safer Neighborhoods Program Yard Signs – To introduce residents to the
  Safer Neighborhoods Program, yard signs encouraging residents to join
  the City’s neighborhood watch program and become a block captain were
  distributed at National Night Out and will be available at other events
  throughout the year. The signs will come in two sizes, allowing residents
  living in both homes and apartments to display them proudly. The signs
  include contact information, so if a resident sees a sign in their
  neighborhood they can contact City Hall to get more information about
  becoming involved in neighborhood watch or becoming a block captain.

  •  In-Person Neighborhood Watch Meetings – In addition to the yard signs,
  staff has coordinated with our public safety officers to resume monthly in-
  person block captain meetings beginning on August 11th.

  •  Officer Drop-Ins at Adult Park Programming – Designed for community
  members that might not attend formal watch meetings or that are hesitant
  to participate in neighborhood watch for various reasons. Scheduling
  officer drop-ins at already existing adult park programming will enable the
  City to provide a more informal avenue to foster relationships with the
  Special Assignment Deputies and feel more comfortable when they may
  need to report matters to law enforcement. Once regular social hours
  resume at the community centers, staff will coordinate the drop-ins with law
  enforcement.

  2) Wellness Vans at City Parks – The City is working with Los Angeles County
  Supervisor Janice Hahn’s Office to have wellness vans conduct regular visits at
  A.J. Padelford Park and Artesia Park. These vans will provide mobile health
  services to check interested residents, particularly our senior population, for
  diabetes, blood pressure, vitals, and other areas of concern.

  3) Home Security and Alarm Rebate Program – As part of its efforts to improve public
  safety in the community, the City offers a Home Security and Alarm Rebate
  Program for Artesia homeowners. Homeowners who purchase an eligible alarm
  system can receive a rebate of up to $250. The program is currently advertised
  on the City’s website and in The Artesian, but staff is working to promote the
  program on other platforms and at upcoming City events to improve awareness
  as part of the Safer Neighborhoods Program.

Emergency Preparedness

  1) Earthquake Preparedness – Keeping neighborhoods safe also involves being
  prepared for emergencies like earthquakes. Staff is working to provide community
  members with the tools and knowledge necessary when encountered with an
  earthquake. This includes the following activities:

  11
   •  Earthquake Preparedness Seminar – Staff plans to work with the Los
  Angeles County Fire Department to provide an in-person seminar to
  educate residents on what to do in case of a large earthquake.
  •  Earthquake Preparedness Toolkit – Staff will promote and make available
  earthquake toolkits provided by ready.gov and Los Angeles County. These
  toolkits are a great resource for community members for family and
  business emergency planning.

  •  Participate in the Great Shake Out– The City will resume participation in
  the Great Shake Out in October 2021 and will encourage all residents,
  businesses, schools, and visitors to take part in the annual earthquake drill
  to practice their preparedness. Additionally, other types of earthquake
  emergency drills will be promoted throughout the year.

  2) Fire Prevention Readiness – Keeping neighborhoods safe also involves being
  prepared for fires. Staff is working to provide residents with the tools and
  knowledge necessary when encountered with a fire. This includes the following
  activities:

  •  Free Smoke Detectors for Residents – Ensuring that community members
  have smoke detectors in their places of residents is a tangible method to
  promote public safety and the Safer Neighborhoods Program. The City is
  working with Los Angeles County Supervisor Janice Hahn’s Office to obtain
  these smoke detectors to provide the free devices to residents. There will
  be a limited supply available to residents on a first-come, first-serve basis.

  •  Fire Prevention Toolkit – Staff will make available the toolkits provided by
  Los Angeles County Fire Department regarding fire prevention measures
  families can use at home and at work.

  3) CERT Training – CERT training covers basic skills that are important to know in a
  disaster when emergency services are not available. With training and practice,
  community members will be able to protect themselves and maximize their
  capability to help neighbors after a disaster. CERT Training programs are offered
  through the Los Angeles County Fire Department and staff is working with
  representatives to implement a training at Artesia Park as soon as the department
  resumes offering the CERT training (it has temporarily been suspended due to
  Covid-19).

Promotion/Advertisement

The Safer Neighborhoods Program will be advertised and promoted at City events
through yard signs and informational flyers. Staff is also preparing a mailer regarding the
Programs to be distributed in September as part of the City’s participation in National
Preparedness Month. Additionally, Program information will be available on the City’s
website and promoted on social media platforms throughout the year.

  12
 FISCAL ANALYSIS:
There is no direct cost to the general fund associated with the Safer Neighborhoods
Program. The City received a discretionary grant from grant from Los Angeles County
Supervisor Hahn’s Office for $5,000 to purchase the yard signs which are available to
advertise the program to the community.

RECOMMENDED COUNCIL ACTION:
Staff recommends the City Council receive and file this informational report.

ATTACHMENTS:
Program Flyer

SUBJECT: Discussion on Amending the Regular Meeting Dates of the Public Safety Commission

BACKGROUND
On March 2019, the City Council adopted Ordinance No. 18-864 which, among other items,
amended Section 2-2.407 of the Artesia Municipal Code regarding the regular meeting
location, date, and time of the Public Safety Commission meetings.

The Section 2-2.407 (Regular Meetings, Time and Place) concerning the Public Safety
Commission currently reads as follows:

  The regular meeting of the Public Safety Commission shall be held at 18747
  Clarkdale Avenue, Artesia, California, unless otherwise specified in the meeting
  notice, on the first Tuesday of January, April, July, and October at the hour of 6:00
  p.m., unless the items of business before the Commission require that adjourned
  regular or special meetings be called more frequently.

The first Tuesday of January and July often conflict with New Years Day and Independence
Day holidays making holding the regular meeting difficult.

ANALYSIS
The Public Safety Commission has not convened since its April 2022 meeting. This is largely
due to the scheduled meeting date falling on the Tuesday after an observed holiday. To ensure
the Commission can adequately perform its responsibilities to the City Council, the scheduled
meeting dates must be amended to prevent conflicts with observed holidays.

Suggested Alternatives:

  1. Amend the regular meetings of the Commission to the fourth Tuesday of January,
  April, July, and October, or
  2. Amend the regular meetings of the Commission to the first Tuesday of February, May,
  August, and November, or
  3. Discuss alternate meeting dates and provide direction.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the Public Safety Commission make a recommendation to City Council
to amend Section 2-2.407 of the Artesia Municipal Code modifying the dates of the regular
meeting of the Public Safety Commission.

SUBJECT: Cancellation of Regularly Scheduled Meeting set for July 4, 2023 and Setting an
  Alternate Meeting Date

BACKGROUND AND RECOMMENDATION
According the Section 2-2.407 of the Artesia Municipal Code, the Regular meeting of the
Public Safety Commission is to be held first Tuesday of January, April, July, and October. The
next regular meeting of the Public Safety Commission falls on July 4, 2023. As July 4th is an
observed holiday, this meeting will be cancelled and it is recommended that the Public Safety
Commission schedule a special meeting on June 27, 2023.
